note: Migration helper that builds Content Sync Pools/Flows from an existing Acquia Content Hub config. It hard-depends on acquia_contenthub, which is NOT installed on this eval site, so the submodule cannot be enabled here. Recipe cases are grounded in its source (forms, drush command content_sync_migrate_acquia_content_hub / mach, default pool machine name 'content'); medium/hard are grounded in the migration's OUTPUT - standard cms_content_sync_pool/flow config entities - which are created and inspected via the parent module's already-enabled config entities without contacting any backend.

evals.prompt: What is the purpose of the cms_content_sync_migrate_acquia_content_hub module, and what Content Sync configuration does it produce?
evals.expected_output: It bootstraps a Content Sync setup from an existing Acquia Content Hub configuration, creating standard cms_content_sync_pool and cms_content_sync_flow config entities (plus EntityStatus records) so a site can move from Acquia Content Hub to Content Sync without configuring syndication from scratch.

evals.prompt: Which Drush command does cms_content_sync_migrate_acquia_content_hub provide (and its alias), and which options are required to run it?
When cms_content_sync_migrate_acquia_content_hub runs its migration, what is the machine name of the default Content Sync Pool it creates?
evals.expected_output: The default pool machine name is 'content' (label 'Content') - MigrationBase::DEFAULT_POOL_MACHINE_NAME, created via Pool::createPool().

evals.prompt: This site already holds the Content Sync Pool that a migration from Acquia Content Hub would produce, under the machine id ccs_ach_pool. Inspect the live configuration and report that pool's backend (Sync Core) URL.
evals.expected_output: The Pool ccs_ach_pool has backend_url https://acquia-migrated.content-sync.example (config cms_content_sync.pool.ccs_ach_pool).

evals.prompt: The cms_content_sync_migrate_acquia_content_hub module normally produces a Content Sync Pool and Flow from an Acquia Content Hub config. Reproduce that output manually on this site: create a cms_content_sync Pool with machine id 'ccs_ach_pool' (label 'CCS ACH Pool', backend_url 'https://acquia-migrated.content-sync.example') and a cms_content_sync Flow with machine id 'ccs_ach_flow' (name 'CCS ACH Flow', type 'both', variant 'simple'). Apply both to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A cms_content_sync_pool ccs_ach_pool (backend_url https://acquia-migrated.content-sync.example) and a cms_content_sync_flow ccs_ach_flow (variant 'simple') both exist, mirroring what MigrationBase creates via Pool::createPool()/createFlow().
